text.p: Celtic were denied the chance of closing the gap on Glasgow rivals Rangers at the top of the Scottish premier division on Tuesday night when snow caused a late postponment of their game at Dunfermline.
A victory for Tommy Burns' side at East End Park would have reduced the deficit at the top to two points.
Snow also led to the postponment of two of the other four games in Scotland with Clyde against Stranraer and Cowdenbeath versus Forfar falling victim to the weather.

The first division match between East Fife and Dundee was abandoned after 47 minutes because of a floodlight failure when Dundee were leading 2-1. No new date has yet been fixed for the re-scheduled matches.
